objective: Build a polished, compact Godot puzzle vertical slice where direct manipulation of one continuous rope teaches a reusable knot language and culminates in a surprising machine-like puzzle.

nodes.instructions: Explore implementable 2D rope and knot puzzle grammars for this exact Godot scope. Compare winding, crossing order, tension, contact sequences, and authored anchors. Propose a small language that can recombine surprisingly without demanding mathematically perfect knot simulation.

Explore interaction feel, teaching, visual feedback, accessibility, and audio for direct rope manipulation. Identify the smallest set of signals that makes grabbing, pinning, threading, tension, failure, and success legible.

Develop contrasting five-to-ten-minute level arcs using one rope. Seek an earned machine-like finale and avoid a mere sequence of silhouette tracing tasks. Keep implementation feasible in one compact Godot project.

Synthesize one candidate-specific vertical slice. Choose a coherent topology model, teaching sequence, interaction contract, visual direction, deterministic test strategy, and bounded implementation plan. Preserve creative conviction instead of averaging every scout idea.

Implement the complete playable vertical slice in the mutable paths. Run Godot import/headless checks. Preserve deterministic factory hooks whose score derives from observed simulation state. Prefer a cohesive finished slice over unused framework.

Inspect and test the implementation for rope stability, topology false positives, reset/progression failures, boundary violations, and honest factory metrics. Return outcome pass or revise with concrete evidence.

Review the playable sequence for clarity, tactile feedback, pacing, visual coherence, and whether the finale genuinely recombines the learned rope language. Do not claim fun without a human playtest. Return outcome pass or revise with prioritized findings.
